## sWGS fitting

- Fitting copy number to absolute state has continued to be a (often overlooked) challenge.
- Methods applied to sWGS are particularly limited due to lack of SNP information
- Resulting fits are often mathematically invariant and/or only qualitatively different

```{r swgs_fits,fig.width=12}
britroc_swgS <- read.table("britroc_30kb_ds_absCopyNumber_segmentTable.tsv",sep = "\t",header = T)
britroc_swgS_meta <- read.table("britroc_30kb_ds_abs_fits.tsv",header = T,sep = "\t") %>%
    rename(sample = SAMPLE_ID)

plot.sample <- unique(britroc_swgS$sample)[5]
cn.data <- britroc_swgS[britroc_swgS$sample == plot.sample,]

cn.data.refit <- CINfits::rescaleFit(cn.data,new_ploidy = 2.2,new_purity = 0.55,old_purity = 0.83)

par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plotProfile(cn.data,sample = plot.sample,purity = 0.83)
plotProfile(cn.data.refit,sample = plot.sample,purity = 0.55)
```

__Current process__

- perform grid search
- collapse ploidy-purity combinations in proximity with same loss
- Select Top 10 lowest loss solutions for each sample
- Remove overlapping solutions
- manually curate solutions to pick best

```{r sunrise}
plotSunrise(cn.data,purity = 0.83,) +
    ggtitle("CN profile fitting loss grid search") +
    labs(fill="loss (MAD)") + theme(legend.position = "right") +
    geom_point(aes(x="3.3",y = "0.83"),color="green",size = 3) +
    geom_point(aes(x="2.2",y = "0.55"),color="red",size = 3)
```

## Predicting fit quality

### Features

Selection is both quantitative and qualitative

```{r CIN_features}
calculateCINStats(cn.data)
```

Use of `QDNASeq` input also allows for the computation of segment variance which is leveraged in the swgs-absolutecn pipeline

```{r qdnaseq,echo=FALSE}
rdsdata <- readRDS("../../../../OneDrive - CRUK Cambridge Institute/britroc-cn-analysis/absolute_POST_down_sampling/britroc_30kb_ds_absCopyNumber.rds")
```

```{r qdnaseqPlot}
plot(rdsdata[,"IM_202"],doCalls=FALSE,showSD=TRUE,logTransform=FALSE,ylim=c(0,8),ylab="Absolute tumour CN")
abline(h=1:9,col = "blue")
```

```{r data}
## Load and pre-process data
cellQC <- read.table("britroc_multifit_meta.tsv",header = T,sep = "\t") %>% 
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    dplyr::select(-grid_ploidy) %>%
    dplyr::rename(purity = grid_purity) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(use = factor(use))

cellQcLong <- cellQC %>% 
                tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -c(1,ncol(.)),names_to = "features")
```

The quantitative features can be computed for each fit and include a class label as to whether I determined the fit was good or not

```{r features}
knitr::kable(head(cellQC))
```

```{r datapre}
## Data preview
dim(cellQC)
```

### Feature-class distributions

```{r plots}
ggplot(cellQcLong,aes(log(value + .Machine$double.eps),colour=use)) +
    geom_density() +
    facet_wrap(. ~ features,scales = "free") +
    theme_bw()
```

### correlated predictors

```{r corr,warning=FALSE}
corrMat <- cor(as.matrix(cellQC[,c(2:7)]),method = "spearman")
testRes = corrplot::cor.mtest(as.matrix(cellQC[,c(2:7)]),method = "spearman", conf.level = 0.95)
corrplot::corrplot(corr = corrMat,p.mat = testRes$p, method = 'number',type="upper")
```

### Running model fitting

```{r datasplit}
## Perform data split using 70/20/10 split and stratified sampling to balance outcome class
dataTrainTest <- splitFittingData(cellQC,prop = 0.7,strata = "use")
dataSplit <- dataTrainTest$dataSplit

## Set training and test data sets
trainingData <- dataTrainTest$trainingData
testingData <- dataTrainTest$testingData
```

```{r training}
kable(head(trainingData))
```

```{r testing}
kable(head(trainingData))
```

```{r outcomeBalance}
## Check class balance
table(trainingData$use,dnn = "training") / sum(table(trainingData$use))
table(testingData$use,dnn = "testing") / sum(table(testingData$use))
```

```{r setmodelreceipe}
## Set recipe for model
# update sample column to be ID rather than predictor
modelRecipeCV <- makeModelRecipe(data = trainingData,folds = 10,strata = "use")
modelRecipe <- modelRecipeCV$recipe

summary(modelRecipe)
```

#### Set cross-fold validation

```{r CVfolds}
## Set number of folds for cross-validation in training set
folds <- modelRecipeCV$cv
folds
```

#### set optimisation metric

```{r optmetric}
opt_metric <- "pr_auc"
opt_metric
```

#### RBF SVM

```{r svmModel,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#set RBF svm
final_linsvm_res <- fitSVM(data = dataSplit,
                           model = modelRecipe,
                           folds = folds,
                           metric = opt_metric)
```

#### logistic regression

```{r lgModel}
## Set logistic regression with glmnet engine/function
final_lr_res <- fitGLMLogisticRegression(data = dataSplit,
                                         model = modelRecipe,
                                         folds = folds,
                                         mixture = 0.5,
                                         metric = opt_metric)
```

#### Random forest

```{r rfModel}
## Set randomforest
final_rf_res <- fitRandomForest(data = dataSplit,
                                model = modelRecipe,
                                folds = folds,
                                metric = opt_metric,
                                importance = "impurity",
                                trees = 100)
```

#### xbg

```{r setxgbt}
final_xgb_res <- fitXGBtree(data = dataSplit,
                            model = modelRecipe,
                            folds = folds,
                            metric = opt_metric,
                            trees = 100)
```

### Compare models

```{r compare_models}
models <- list(final_lr_res,final_linsvm_res,final_xgb_res,final_rf_res)

modelMetrics <- CINfits:::collateModelMetrics(models = models)
modelROC <- CINfits:::collateModelRoc(models = models,usePR = F)
modelROCPR <- CINfits:::collateModelRoc(models = models,usePR = T)
```

```{r plot_models_table}
modelMetricsTable <- modelMetrics %>%
                        select(-.estimator) %>%
                        mutate(.estimate = round(.estimate,digits = 3)) %>%
                        pivot_wider(names_from = ".metric",id_cols = "model",values_from = ".estimate") %>%
                        arrange(desc(f_meas))


modelMetricsTable %>%
    mutate(across(-model,~cell_spec(.x,bold = ifelse(.x == max(.x),T,F)))) %>%
    kable(escape = FALSE)
```

## Model triage

Models work well for the most part but incorrect assignments still occur in two forms
- High confidence
- Low confidence

```{r explore borders}
rf_table <- final_rf_res %>%
                collect_predictions() %>%
                mutate(prediction_accuracy = ifelse(.pred_class != use,"incorrect","correct")) %>%
                group_by(.row) %>%
                mutate(prob = max(.pred_FALSE,.pred_TRUE))
```

```{r predPlot1}
ggplot(rf_table) +
    geom_density2d(aes(.pred_FALSE,.pred_TRUE,color=prediction_accuracy)) +
    facet_wrap(use ~ prediction_accuracy) +
    theme_bw()
```

```{r predPlot2}
ggplot(rf_table) +
    geom_density(aes(prob,color=prediction_accuracy)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.87,linetype=2) +
    theme_bw()
```

If we predict the correct fit we can flag samples with low confidence assignments based on model probability
and subsequently for samples with 2 or more fits assigned as TRUE, use lowest clonality or segvariance to select the final fit.

```{r triage_profiles}
cellQCTriage <- CINfits:::predictProfile(qctable = cellQC,flagThreshold = 0.84)

head(cellQCTriage)
```

## Phil-in-a-box

__Final process__

- perform grid search
- collapse ploidy-purity combinations in proximity with same loss
- Select Top 10 lowest loss solutions for each sample
- Remove overlapping solutions
- Use model to assign fit as use or not and flag low confidence fits
    - (Optionally perform manual refitting of flagged samples)
